skill.summary: Guides uv-based Python environment setup, dependency management, execution, and publishing.

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are Markdown examples and inline command names, not executable Ruby shell backticks. I confirmed the curl-to-shell installer as critical, confirmed plaintext PyPI token guidance, and noted low supply-chain risks in extra index and unpinned Git dependency examples. No prompt injection text was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell setup with package-manager instructions, verified download steps, or a link to official uv installation documentation.
Prefer trusted publishing and add warnings before any token-based .pypirc example.
Warn about dependency confusion for extra indexes and avoid unpinned Git branch examples.
State that commands must be user-approved, project-scoped, and reviewed before execution.

static_findings.snippet: # Build sdist + wheel — uv has a native builder, no separate `build` install
# Dev tooling → dependency-groups (PEP 735). `uv add --dev <pkg>` writes here;
# `uv sync` installs it by default. Not shipped with the published package.
# Opt-in extras users install explicitly: `uv add "my-package[docs]"`
(`uv add` / `uv sync` / `uv run`) over the `uv pip` compatibility layer — it
manages `pyproject.toml` + a lockfile for you and is reproducible.
| Start a project | `uv init <name>` (app) · `uv init --package <name>` (installable, `src/` layout)
| Add dev dependency | `uv add --dev pytest ruff` |
| Run in project env | `uv run pytest` |
| Install a CLI tool | `uv tool install ruff` · one-shot: `uvx ruff` |
`uv init` creates `pyproject.toml`, pins a Python version, and prepares the
project for `uv add` / `uv sync`. The `--package` (src) layout is preferred for
`uv` creates and manages `.venv` automatically — you rarely activate it; just
uv run -- ruff check .      # `--` ends uv flag parsing
Never call bare `python` / `pytest` / `ruff` in a uv project — they may resolve
to a different interpreter. Always `uv run`.
Use `uv tool` / `uvx` for developer CLIs (ruff, pre-commit, httpie). Use
`uv add` only for things your code imports.
is a sensible floor for new projects (TaskGroup, `Self`, faster interpreter).
# Dev deps live here; `uv add --dev <pkg>` manages this group.
`uv pip` mirrors pip's interface for environments uv doesn't manage (a hand-made
venv, a legacy `requirements.txt`, CI that isn't uv-native). It does **not**
update `pyproject.toml` or the lockfile — prefer `uv add` / `uv sync` whenever
| Pin project Python | `uv init --python 3.12` or edit `requires-python` |
| Lock/resolve conflict | `uv lock --resolution=lowest-direct` to probe, then loosen bounds |
- `uv add` / `uv remove` / `uv sync` for project dependencies (not `uv pip install`)
- `uv run` to execute anything inside the project env
- `uv tool install` / `uvx` for standalone developer CLIs
- `uv pip` only for environments uv doesn't manage

content.value_statement: Python projects often drift across pip, venv, and pyproject workflows. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through uv-based setup, dependency changes, locking, running, and publishing.
actual_capabilities: Creates new app or package projects with uv init guidance.
Adds, removes, syncs, and locks dependencies with uv project commands.
Explains pyproject.toml patterns for runtime, dev, optional, and script dependencies.
Documents uv run, uv tool, and uvx workflows for local execution.
Provides references for private indexes, workspaces, CI cache patterns, and publishing.
Covers TestPyPI, PyPI, changelog, version, and trusted publishing workflows.
limitations: Requires the uv CLI to be installed before commands can run.
Assumes users approve shell commands and review network package sources.
Provides documentation patterns; it does not verify package integrity automatically.
Publishing examples require project-specific credentials, repository settings, and CI permissions.

use_cases.title: Start a Python project
use_cases.description: Create a new uv-managed application or package with a pyproject.toml file and lockfile workflow.

use_cases.title: Standardize team dependencies
use_cases.description: Use uv sync, uv lock, and dependency groups to keep local and CI environments aligned.

use_cases.title: Prepare a package release
use_cases.description: Follow build, TestPyPI, PyPI, changelog, and trusted publishing guidance for a release.

prompt_templates.title: Set up a new project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the python-env skill to create a uv setup plan for a new Python application named atlas. Include Python version, dependencies, and first test command.

prompt_templates.title: Add dependencies safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the python-env skill to add runtime and development dependencies to this project. Explain which uv commands update pyproject.toml and the lockfile.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize an existing project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the python-env skill to move this existing Python project toward uv. Review requirements files, pyproject.toml, lockfile needs, and command changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a package release
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the python-env skill to prepare a release checklist for this package. Include versioning, build checks, TestPyPI validation, and trusted publishing.

output_examples.input: Set up a new uv project for a small CLI tool.
output_examples.output: A short setup plan with project initialization, Python version choice, runtime dependencies, dev tools, lockfile sync, and test execution.

output_examples.input: Review my dependency workflow before CI runs.
output_examples.output: A dependency checklist covering lockfile freshness, dependency groups, uv sync behavior, and commands that should run in CI.
A release workflow covering metadata, build artifacts, validation, TestPyPI installation, production upload, and trusted publishing setup.

best_practices: Use uv project commands first, and reserve uv pip for legacy or unmanaged environments.
Review package sources before using private indexes, Git dependencies, or TestPyPI installs.
Run commands through uv run so tools use the project environment.
anti_patterns: Do not mix bare python, pytest, or ruff commands with a uv-managed project.
Do not copy private index or token examples without adding project-specific security controls.
Do not publish from a dirty or unverified build directory.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps manage Python environments, dependencies, lockfiles, execution, and publishing with uv.

faq.question: Does this skill install uv automatically?
faq.answer: No. The user must install uv and approve any shell commands before use.

faq.question: Can it replace pip workflows?
faq.answer: It recommends uv project workflows for most projects and explains uv pip for legacy cases.

faq.question: Does it support pyproject.toml?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for dependencies, optional dependencies, scripts, tooling, and project metadata.

faq.question: Can it help with package publishing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers build checks, TestPyPI validation, PyPI upload, changelogs, and trusted publishing.

faq.question: What should users review before running commands?
faq.answer: Users should review package names, indexes, Git sources, credentials, and file paths before approving commands.
